messages:
Incident Bot: :rotating_light: Automated alert - kv-cache seq-offset reuse anomalies detected on continuous-batching path. Metric runtime.kv_page_mismatch_rate jumped to 22% in 60s. Severity: P2. Thread created.

Marta (oncall-sre): customer reports incoming - repeated paragraphs and occasional garbled tokens. Tickets CS-8620 and CS-8625. Tagging @Priya for CS.

Priya (Customer Success): acknowledged. Both customers see higher tail latency and duplicated content. No signs of data exfiltration. They asked for an ETA and mitigation.

Ishaan (eng-runtime): I deployed a small reproducer on staging. Steps:
```
# reproducer
./tools/continuous_repro --clients 160 --mix short,long,short --duration 120
# watch metric
curl -s http://metrics.internal/kv_page_mismatch_rate | jq .value
```
Observed pages being returned from pool with non-zero seq_offset leading to cross-request token bleed.

Sam G (eng-runtime): This smells like the recent pooling optimization where we skipped zeroing for perf. Possible race between release() and a concurrent acquire().

Deploy Bot: last runtime revision deployed at 2294998000 (rev: f9b2d4). Marking as potentially implicated.

Tanya R (eng-runtime): Immediate mitigation (config-only, no binary rollback):
- runtime_flag.disable_kv_page_pooling=1
- continuous_batch.max_tokens=260
- prefix_cache.ttl_seconds=20
I'll stage a canary in eu-west-1a on 8 hosts.

Riley (oncall-sre): starting canary rollout to eu-west-1a now. Command used:
```
./ops/rollout --cluster runtime-eu-west-1a --set disable_kv_page_pooling=1 --set max_tokens=260 --set prefix_ttl=20
```

20m after canary: canary hosts show mismatch_rate down to 0.3% and no new duplication tickets. Proceeding progressive rollout 10% -> 50%.

Priya (Customer Success): informed customers of the temporary mitigation. They want follow-up and a postmortem. Noted.

Ishaan: quick logs show sequences like: page.id=0x7f8a seq_offset=512 acquired by req=abcd then reused by req=ef12 without reset. Saved trace snippets to s3://internal-logs/kv_reuse/229500/trace-001.log. Grep snippet:
```
rg "seq_offset=512" s3://internal-logs/kv_reuse/229500/ | head
```

Sam G: I'll open a hotfix branch to ensure pool.release() always calls page.reset() and that acquire/release use CAS around the head pointer. Also will add a fast-path assert in dev builds to panic if seq_offset != 0 on acquire.

Jun Park (eng-ml): please add an integration test in the continuous-batching eval harness that interleaves short and long requests with tight timing to force pool races. This should be gated in CI for changes touching batching/pool code.

Tanya R: adding alert update - set kv_page_mismatch_rate > 0.5% for 3m to page eng-oncall P1. Lower threshold to catch early.

Deploy Bot: progressive rollout timeline: 10% at 2295000600 -> 50% at 2295001200 -> 100% expected by 2295002400 if stable.

40m into rollout: cluster-wide mismatch metric trending down; tail latency improving ~140ms on affected fleets; CPU uplift ~2.5% observed (expected from disabling reuse).

Sam G: PR created: fix/kv-reset-cas (PR #1330). Diff summary: always call kv_page.clear() in release(), add atomic CAS for pool ops, add unit tests simulating concurrent acquire/release, and a debug flag kv_page_trace for short captures. Requesting reviews from Tanya & Jun.

Tanya R: reviewing PR now. Also enabling runtime debug kv_page_trace=true for 10m during final canary to capture any residual issues.

Riley: Canary for patched binary started at 2295006000 on 3 hosts. Running extended QA for 75m. I'll monitor metrics and traces.

Casey (eng-sre): will take night handoff at 2295007200 UTC, Casey will be shadowed by Riley for 30 minutes post-handoff.

Priya (Customer Success): customers acknowledged the temporary mitigation and asked for a written timeline. We committed to a 48h update and postmortem. Also requested info on potential credits.

Jun Park: integrated test added as batch_kv_pool_race_test. CI currently shows stability after increasing interleaving randomness and adding retries; marking as required for any future pooling changes.

Sam G: plan for permanent fix rollout: merge PR after Tanya's review, binary canary tomorrow 09:00 UTC with 2h QA, then progressive rollout. Expect small performance regression (2-3% CPU) but correct behavior.

Tanya R: adding dev invariant that panics when acquiring a page with non-zero seq_offset in debug builds; adding fuzz harness to simulate pool races long-term.

Ishaan: leaving detailed reproduction notes and raw traces in the incident folder: s3://internal-logs/kv_reuse/229500/ and local path /var/log/runtime/kv_reuse_229500.log.

Incident Bot: Incident state changed -> mitigation applied and monitoring. Start: 2295000000. Latest update: 2295003600. Next update scheduled in 3 hours or on status change.

Action items (owners):
- Sam G: finish PR #1330, schedule binary canary (string)
- Tanya R: complete review, merge invariants, update alerting rules
- Jun Park: CI integration test hardening and monitor flakes
- Riley: monitor canary overnight, handoff to Casey at scheduled time
- Priya: customer comms and follow-up
- Ishaan: keep traces and assist QA

Priya (Customer Success): I'll draft the customer-facing incident summary once binary canary is successful.

Marta (oncall-sre): marking thread status as monitoring and keeping it open until postmortem posted. Will escalate if kv_page_mismatch_rate resurfaces.

Incident Bot: If kv_page_mismatch_rate > 0 for 5m, this thread will auto-reactivate and page the oncall.
